messages:
anil: heads up — after the batching heuristics roll (prefetch_v2) we saw a sharp surge in cache-proxy -> backend QPS. 5xxs on cache-proxy started at ~21:34 UTC. looks like miss amplification rather than backend latency.

ops-bot: ALERT: cache-proxy errors > 5% for service=kv-cache (21:34:12 UTC). rolling window 1m. ticket #INC-4592 created.

maria: putting numbers on it — what hit-rate delta are we seeing?

anil: quick stats from the window 21:32-21:36:
- global prefix hit rate: 91.8% -> 48.6%
- hot-prefix cohort (top 1k keys): 95% -> 61%
- backend RPS increased x3 from normal per-shard baseline

kevin: logs show a pattern where key normalization changed for short prompts after the roll. new keying strips trailing "\n" from user prompts which causes previously-cached variants to miss. snippet from proxy logs:
```
[21:33:58] GET /kv/hot -- key=prompt::user123::v2::trimmed:true
[21:33:58] MISS upstream fetch shard=us-west-2-a id=14 latency=12ms
```
\nkevin: also saw prefetch controller queue latency spike at the same time — prefetch workers started fanout to many shards which overloaded a couple of older nodes.

sophia: can we confirm whether kernel selection/batching change touched the key-normalization path? that seems like a weird coupling.

anil: yes — the batching PR moved normalization into the front of the tokenization pipeline to dedupe compute across micro-batches. missed a subtle config flag that toggles "preserve_newline" for legacy keys. that explains the sudden keyspace shift.

maria: action plan: 1) flip prefetche_v2 off (quick rollback), 2) throttle proxy fanout to stay under 2x baseline, 3) run a migration to reindex trimmed keys -> legacy namespace.

kevin: I pushed a hotfix to ops API to disable prefetch_v2:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/features -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' -d '{"feature":"prefetch_v2","enabled":false}'
```
ops-bot: Feature toggle update accepted — prefetch_v2 disabled (21:38:10 UTC).

anil: after disable we saw backend QPS fall back to ~1.1x baseline in ~90s. error rate dropped under 1%. hit-rate climbed to ~88% in hot cohort (taking into account some in-flight evictions). :thumbsup:

sophia: follow-ups: 1) add unit + e2e tests for newline-preservation keying, 2) decouple key-normalization from batch kernel selection so a change in batching can't alter cache keys, 3) add a short-circuit in prefetch to limit shard fanout when miss-rate > 10%.

maria: I'm going to file RFC for the decoupling work and put a guard in canary rollout checklist. also schedule a postmortem doc with timelines and exact metric graphs.

anil: timeline note for postmortem: root cause = normalization flag regression in batching refactor; contributing cause = prefetch fanout + older shard capacity skew; mitigation = emergency toggle + temporary proxy fanout throttle; long-term = reindex + code decoupling.

kevin: curious note from profiler: kernel selection latency decreased 8% in steady-state, so batching change did help perf but regressed operational correctness. worth redoing with keying invariant tests.

sophia: +1 for invariant tests. can we also add a canary probetest that simulates hot-prefix churn to catch fanout storms?

maria: filing postmortem and adding owners. assigning long-term work to @anil (keying decouple), @kevin (prefetch safety), @sophia (canary tests).

anil: thanks — will take ownership.

kevin: one last note: for the reindex migration let's do it shard-by-shard with rate limit and use deterministic mapping so we don't create duplicates. I'll draft the migration script.

ops-bot: INC-4592 updated: status=mitigated, owner=anil, followups=PMT-1023 (postmortem), ENG-2041 (reindex).
